ratings_why.fun: Phase lines read at a glance and the Full spike is a joy to plan for, but five rule ideas and borrowed text on every Hare make the board slow to read mid-game.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because time itself is the tribe's resource: a public Moon you bend, plus Full turning Hares into copies of other tribes' engines, plays unlike any of today's six tribes.

verdict_why: One real readability fix remains (Moon-Scour stacking through borrowed copies); otherwise the v2 wording is clean.

points.text: The Moon-Scour doesn't say whether a Changeling that borrows its text adds a second doubling (x4), or whether it doubles its own borrowed copy. The Hare in the Moon got a no-stack line; this needs the same.
Dame Waxwell says 'you choose... or holds' but the Moon can't hold two turns running; say the hold option is missing after a hold, so a player isn't offered a choice that fails.
The Three Hares could say what happens when the slot just before or after is empty (no unit, or skip to the next), since Bramble's gaps never close.
The fantasy lands in what cards do: boxing bouts, the lonely leveret, the three hares sharing gains, witches in borrowed shapes. Keep the flavour-to-rule mapping as it is.
Hare in Her Form is still the longest card in the tribe; a keyword for 'can't be attacked while it has a row-mate' would make it read in one glance.

standouts.why: Three words of text, and it turns the Hare into the witch in borrowed shape next to your best off-tribe unit.
Reads instantly and tells the second-litter story while feeding triples.
The short charm made literal: Waxing jumps to Full and the whole coven changes shape.

weakest.why: Two clauses and an exception; the stillness-then-bolt idea is lovely but hard to read at a glance.
What she becomes depends on the enemy's card text, which the player must read off another board mid-fight.
Text works one fight in four; a plain body most of the game.

flags.note: Stacking with borrowed copies of itself is unstated.
Box again on each win can chain through a weak board at Start of Combat, growing each time; Full with the Moon-Scour makes it +4/+4 a win.
Golden Hare in the Moon with golden Waxwell and Mad March Hare is the designer's own 270-stats-a-turn ceiling.
